questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A: When you squeeze one end of a tube to get toothpaste out from the other end, Pascal’s principle is observed.

Reason R: A change in the pressure applied to an enclosed incompressible fluid is transmitted undiminished to every portion of the fluid and to the walls of its container.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is not correct but R is correct
A is correct but R is not correct
Both A and R is correct and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Pascal's law states that the pressure in a closed incompressible fluid is transmitted equally in all directions.

The formula for pressure is given by

$P = \dfrac{F}{A}$

When a toothpaste is squeezed let the pressure transmitted by $P$. At the mouth of the toothpaste the pressure will also be equal to $P$~due to Pascal's law.~The pressure applied to the tube is transmitted equally throughout the toothpaste. When the pressure reaches the open end, it forces toothpaste out through the opening. Hence, both~$A \text{ and } R$~is correct and~$R$ is correct explanation for~ $A$.

questions.q: The top of a water tank is open to air and its water level is maintained. It is giving out $0.74m^{3}$ water per minute through a circular opening of $2$ cm radius in its wall. The depth of the centre of the opening from the level of water in the tank is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Volume of water flowing out$= Av$, where~$A$~is area of opening and~$v$~is speed of water from the opening.

$\text{Volume} = \pir^{2}v$

$0 . 74\left(\dfrac{m^{3}}\min\right) = \left(3.14 \times \left(2 \times {10}^{- 2}\right)2 \times \sqrt{2 \times 10 \times H}\right)\dfrac{m3}{s} \times \dfrac{60s}\min$

$⇒ H = {\left(\dfrac{0.74}{60 \times 3.14 \times 4 \times {10}^{- 4}}\right)}^{2} \times \dfrac{1}{20}$

$⇒ H = 4.8m$

Hence, the height of water in the tank was~$4 . 8m$& from the bottom of the tank.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): Clothes containing oil or grease stains cannot be cleaned by water wash.

Reason (R) : Because the angle of contact between the oil/ grease and water is obtuse. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the option given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Angle of contact between oil and water is obtuse i.e., greater than critical angle of contact& \left(\thetac > 90 °\right)$, therefore they do not stick and that's the reason grease/oil stains can not be removed by water wash.&

Thus, both& (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

$

questions.q: A cube of ice floats partly in water and partly in kerosene oil. The ratio of volume of ice immersed in water to that in kerosene oil (specific gravity of Kerosene oil $=0.8$, specific gravity of ice $=0.9$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{v}_1=\text { volume immersed in water. } \\ & \mathrm{v}_2=\text { volume immersed in oil. } \\ & \mathrm{v}_1 \rho_{\mathrm{w}} \mathrm{g}+\mathrm{v}_2 \rho_{\mathrm{o}} \mathrm{g}=\left(\mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{v}_2\right) \rho_{\mathrm{c}} \mathrm{g} \\ & \mathrm{v}_1+\frac{\mathrm{v}_2 \rho_{\mathrm{o}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{w}}}=\left(\mathrm{v}_1+\mathrm{v}_2\right) \frac{\rho_{\mathrm{c}}}{\rho_{\mathrm{w}}} \\ & =\mathrm{v}_1+0.8 \mathrm{v}_2=0.9 \mathrm{v}_1+0.9 \mathrm{v}_2 \\ & =0.1 \mathrm{v}_1=0.1 \mathrm{v}_2 \\ & \mathrm{v}_1: \mathrm{v}_2=1: 1\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A soap bubble, blown by a mechanical pump at the mouth of a tube increases in volume with time at a constant rate. The graph that correctly depicts the time dependence of pressure inside the bubble is given by:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\dfrac{dV}{dt} = k$

$⇒ V = kt$

$⇒ \dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3} = kt$

$⇒ r = {\left(\dfrac{3k}{4\pi}\right)}^{\dfrac{1}{3}}t^{\dfrac{1}{3}}$

$P - {P}_{0} = \dfrac{4T}{r}$

$⇒ P - {P}_{0} = 4T . \left(\dfrac{3k}{4\pi}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} . \dfrac{1}{t\dfrac{1}{3}}⇒ P = 4T . \left(\dfrac{3k}{4\pi}\right)\dfrac{1}{3} . \dfrac{1}{t\dfrac{1}{3}} + {P}_{0}$

questions.q: In Millikan's oil drop experiment, what is viscous force acting on an uncharged drop of radius $2 . 0 \times {10}^{- 5}m$ and density $1 . 2 \times {10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$?~Take viscosity of liquid $= 1 . 8 \times {10}^{- 5}Nsm^{- 2} .$ (Neglect buoyancy due to air).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Use the concept the viscous force is the same as the weight of the body,&

$⇒ F = mg = ρ \times \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pir^{3}\right) \times g = 3 . 9 \times {10}^{- 10}N$.&

questions.q: A leak proof cylinder of length $1m,$ made of a metal which has very low coefficient of expansion is floating vertically in water at ${0}^{o}C$ such that its height above the water surface is $20cm .$ When the temperature of water is increased to ${4}^{o}C,$ the height of the cylinder above the water surface becomes $21cm .$ The density of water at $T = {4}^{o}C,$ relative to the density at $T = {0}^{o}C$ is close to:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to Archemedes Principle, weight of the body is balanced by the upward thrust force due to buoyancy.

At& $0 ° C$,~$mg = A ( 100 - 20 ) {ρ}_{0 ° C}g$, where~$A$~is area of cross-section of cylinder and~${ρ}_{0 ° C}$~is density of water at~$0 ° C$.
At~$4 ° C$,~$mg = A ( 100 - 21 ) {ρ}_{4 ° C}g$, where~${ρ}_{4 ° C}$~is density of water at~$4 ° C$.
$\dfrac{{ρ}_{4 ° C}}{{ρ}_{0 ° C}} = \dfrac{80}{79} = 1.01$

questions.q:
A fully loaded boeing aircraft has a mass of $5 . 4 \times {10}^{5}kg$. Its total wing area is $500m^{2}$. It is in level flight with a speed of $1080kmh^{- 1}$. If the density of air $ρ$~is $1 . 2kgm^{– 3}$, the fractional increase in the speed of the air on the upper surface of the wing relative to the lower surface in percentage will be

($g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Required lift force,& $F = {P}_{2}A - {P}_{1}A = 5 . 4 \times {10}^{5} \times g$

$⇒ {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \dfrac{5 . 4 \times {10}^{6}}{500} = 5 . 4 \times 2 \times {10}^{3}$

$= 10 . 8 \times {10}^{3}$

Now applying~Bernoulli's Theorem we get

${P}_{2} + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{2}^{2} = {P}_{1} + 0 + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{V}_{1}^{2}$

$⇒ {P}_{2} - {P}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({V}_{1}^{2} - {V}_{2}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ \left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right)\left({V}_{1} + {V}_{2}\right) \left[\text{Since for small change}, {V}_{1} = {V}_{2} =V = 1080kmh^{- 1} = 300ms^{- 1}\right]$

$⇒ 10 . 8 \times {10}^{3} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times1 . 2\left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right) \times2 \times300$

$⇒ 10 . 8 \times10 = 3 . 6 \left({V}_{1} - {V}_{2}\right)

$⇒ {V}_{1} - {V}_{2} = 30$

Therefore, fractional increase will be\left(\dfrac{{V}_{1} - {V}_{2}}{V}) \times100 = \dfrac{30}{300} \times100 = 10 %

$

questions.q: A pressure-pump has a horizontal tube of cross-sectional area $10{cm}^{2}$ for the outflow of water at a speed of $20ms^{- 1}$. The force exerted on the vertical wall just in front of the tube which stops water horizontally flowing out of the tube, is: [given : density of water $= 1000kgm^{- 3}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Volume of water coming out of the pipe per sec& $= Av = 10 \times {10}^{- 4} \times 20 = 0 . 02m^{3}s^{- 1}$

Mass of water hitting the wall per second~$m = 0 . 02 \times {10}^{3} = 20kgs^{- 1}$

As the water hits the wall normal to the wall and stops, the change of momentum of water hitting the wall is~$= m\left(0 - \left(- v\right)\right) = mv$

$= 20 \times 20 = 400kgms^{- 2}$

Since, the change of momentum obtained is per unit time, it is same as the force. ~

Thus, the force acting on the wall by water =~force experienced by water jet$= 400N$.

questions.q: Two cylindrical vessels of equal cross-sectional area $16{cm}^{2}$~contain water upto heights $100$ cm and $150$ cm respectively. The vessels are interconnected so that the water levels in them become equal. The work done by the force of gravity during the process, is [Take density of water $= {10}^{3}kgm^{- 3}$ and $g = 10{ms}^{- 2}$]
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initially, the centre of mass of the right column will be at height of& $75$ cm~and the centre of mass of the left column will be at~$50$ cm. After opening of the valve both columns will have height of~$125$ cm~and their centre of mass will be at height~$\dfrac{125}{2}cm$.~Therefore,

$W = - ∆ U = - \left[\left({m}_{1} + {m}_{2}\right)g\dfrac{{h}_{1} + {h}_{2}}{4} - {m}_{1}g\dfrac{h1}{2} - {m}_{2}g\dfrac{h2}{2}\right]$

Now,~${m}_{1} = ρA{h}_{1}$~and~${m}_{2} = ρA{h}_{2}$

Putting~$ρ = 1000kgm^{- 3}, g = 10ms^{- 2}, {h}_{1} = 100cm, {h}_{2} = 150cm$~and~$A = 16 \times {10}^{- 4}m^{2}$,~we get,

$W = 1J$

questions.q: A small liquid drop of radius $R$ is divided into $27$ identical liquid drops. If the surface tension is $T$, then the work done in the process will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Let radius of the newly formed drops be $r$.

As total volume will remain constant, therefore

$\dfrac{4}{3}\piR^{3} = 27 \times \left(\dfrac{4}{3} \times \pir^{3}\right)

$⇒ R^{3} = 27r^{3}$

$⇒ R = 3r$

$⇒ r = $\dfrac{R}{3}

$⇒ r^{2} = $\dfrac{R2}{9}

Now, work done $= T $\times \Delta$A$

$= T\left[$27\left($4\pir^{2}\right)\right] - T\left[$4\piR^{2}\right] = T \left[27 \lleft(4\pi\dfrac{R2}{9}\right)] --T\left[$4\piR^{2}\right] = T\piR^{2}\left(12 - 4\right)$

$= 8\piR^{2}T$

$

questions.q: Two identical cylindrical vessels are kept on the ground and each contain the same liquid of density $d$. The area of the base of both vessels is $S$ but the height of liquid in one vessel is~${x}_{1}$~and in the other~${x}_{2}$. When both cylinders are connected through a pipe of negligible volume very close to the bottom, the liquid flows from one vessel to the other until it comes to equilibrium at a new height. The change in energy of the system in the process is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Initial height of liquid in container's of same cross section are& ${x}_{1}$ and~${x}_{2}$ respectively. Now value is opened find loss in potential energy when water level be become same

loss in~$PE = {U}_{i} - {U}_{f}$

$= \left[ρ ( A ) {x}_{1}\dfrac{x1}{2} + {ρAx}_{2}\dfrac{x2}{2}\right]g - \left[ρA\left(\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2}}{2}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{{x}_{1} + {x}_{2}}{4}\right) \times 2\right]g$

$= ρAg\left[{x}_{1}^{2}2 + {x}_{2}^{2}2 - \dfrac{\left({x}_{1} + {x}_{1}\right)2}{4}\right] = \dfrac{ρAg\left({x}_{1} - {x}_{2}\right)2}{4}$&

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water.
Statement II : If a capillary tube is immersed first in cold water and then in hot water, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in cold water.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For water, the surface tension decreases as the temperature increases. At higher temperatures, the water molecules have more kinetic energy and are better able to overcome the cohesive forces at the surface, resulting in a decrease in surface tension.

So, the height of capillary rise will be smaller in hot water and larger in cold water.

Hence, statement I is true, but statement II is false.

questions.q: Eight equal drops of water are falling through air with a steady speed of $10cms^{- 1}$. If the drops coalesce, the new velocity is:-
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The terminal velocity can be given by&

${v}_{T} = \dfrac{2 ( ρ - \sigma ) r^{2}g}{9η}$.

Clearly,~${v}_{T} ∝ r^{2}$

Let the radius of the small drops be~${r}_{1}$~and the radius of the big drop be~${r}_{2}$.

So,

~$8\left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right){r}_{1}^{3} = \left(\dfrac{4\pi}{3}\right){r}_{2}^{3} ⇒ {r}_{1} = \dfrac{r2}{2}$

Hence, taking the ratio
$\dfrac{\left({v}_{T}\right)1}{\left({v}_{T}\right)2} = \left(\dfrac{r1}{r2}\right)2$
$⇒ \dfrac{10}{\left({v}_{T}\right)2} = \dfrac{1}{4}$
$⇒ \left({v}_{T}\right)2 = 40cms^{- 1}$

questions.q:
A 400 g solid cube having an edge of length 10 cm floats in water. How much volume of the cube is outside the water ?
(Given : density of water $=1000 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-3}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Volume of cube inside water
$\begin{aligned}
& =\left(\frac{\text { Denslty of cube }}{\text { Denslty of water }}\right) \times \text { Volume of cube } \\
& =\frac{\text { Mass of cube }}{\text { Denslty of water }} \\
& =\frac{400 \mathrm{gm}}{1 \mathrm{gm} / \mathrm{cm}^3} \\
& =400 \mathrm{~cm}^3
\end{aligned}$
Volume of cube outside water
$\begin{aligned}
& =\text { Volume of cube }- \text { Volume of cube inside water } \\
& =1000 \mathrm{~cm}^3-400 \mathrm{~cm}^3 \\
& =600 \mathrm{~cm}^3
\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Consider a cylindrical tank of radius $1m$ is filled with water. The top surface of water is at $15m$ from the bottom of the cylinder. There is a hole on the wall of cylinder at a height of $5m$ from the bottom. A force of $5 × {10}^{5}N$ is applied an the top surface of water using a piston. The speed of efflux from the hole will be :
(given atmospheric pressure ${P}_{A} = 1 . 01 × {10}^{5}Pa$, density of water ${ρ}_{w} = 1000kgm^{- 3}$ and gravitational acceleration $g = 10ms^{- 2}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Assuming there is no atmospheric pressure on piston,& ${P}_{1} = \dfrac{F}{\piR^{2}}$~and~${P}_{2} = {P}_{0}$.

Applying Bernoulli's equation at point~$1$~and~$2$,

${p}_{1} + ρg{h}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{1}^{2} = {p}_{2} + ρg{h}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ \left(\dfrac{F}{\piR^{2}}\right) + ρg\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right) = {P}_{0} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v}_{2}^{2}$

$⇒ {v}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2F}{\piR^{2}ρ} - \dfrac{2{P}_{0}}{ρ} + 2g\left({h}_{1} - {h}_{2}\right)}$

${v}_{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2 \times \left(5 \times {10}^{5}\right)}{3 . 14 \times {1}^{2} \times 1000} - \dfrac{2 \times 1 . 01 \times {10}^{5}}{1000} + 2 \times 10 \times 10}$

$\approx 17 . 8ms^{- 1}$

$Mercury is filled in a tube of radius $2 \mathrm{~cm}$ up to a height of $30 \mathrm{~cm}$. The force exerted by mercury on the bottom of the tube is _____ N.
(Given, atmospheric pressure $=10^5 \mathrm{Nm}^{-2}$, density of mercury $=1.36 \times 10^4 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^{-}  \left.{ }^3, $\mathrm{~g}=$10 $\mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-2}, \pi=\frac{22}{7}\right)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{F}=\mathrm{P}_0 \mathrm{~A}+\rho_{\mathrm{m}} \mathrm{ghA} \\ & =10^5 \times \frac{22}{7} \times\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2 \\ & +1.36 \times 10^4 \times 10 \times\left(30 \times 10^{-2}\right)\left(\frac{22}{7} \times\left(2 \times 10^{-2}\right)^2\right) \\ & \mathrm{F}=51.29+125.71=177 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: An ideal fluid of density $800kgm^{- 3}$, flows smoothly through a bent pipe (as shown in figure) that tapers in cross-sectional area from a to $\dfrac{a}{2}$. The pressure difference between the wide and narrow sections of pipe is $4100Pa$. At wider section, the velocity of fluid is $\dfrac{x}{6}\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm\mathrm{ms}^{-1}$ for $x =_____ . (Given $g = 10{ms}^{- 2})
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
From equation of continuity,

$a{v}_{1} = \dfrac{a}{2}{v}_{2} ⇒ {v}_{2} = 2{v}_{1}$

From Bernoulli's theorem,

${P}_{1} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v1}^{2} + ρg{h}_{1} = {P}_{2} + \dfrac{1}{2}ρ{v2}^{2} + ρg{h}_{2} ⇒ {P}_{1} - {P}_{2} = ρ\left[g\left({h}_{2} - {h}_{1}\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}\left({v2}^{2} - {v1}^{2}\right)\right] ⇒ 4100 = 800\left[10\left(- 1\right) + \dfrac{1}{2}3{v1}^{2}\right] ⇒ \dfrac{4100}{800} + 10 = \dfrac{3}{2}{v1}^{2} ⇒ {v}_{1} = \sqrt{\dfrac{121}{4 \times 3}} = \dfrac{363}{6}ms^{- 1}$

Therefore,~$x = 363$.

questions.q: A plane is in level flight at constant speed and each of its two wings has an area of $40m^{2} .$ If the speed of the air is $180kmh^{- 1}$ over the lower wing surface and $252kmh^{- 1}$ over the upper wing surface, the mass of the plane is ________kg .$ (Take air density to be $1kgm^{– 3}$ and $g = 10ms^{– 2})
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Total wing span area, $A = 2 \times 40 = 80m^{2}$

Using Bernoulli's equation, we get uplift force as

$A\left({P}_{2} - {P}_{1}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}ρ\left({V}_{1}^{2} - {V}_{2}^{2}\right)A$

$⇒ mg = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1\left({70}^{2} - {50}^{2}\right) \times 80$

$⇒ mg = 2400 \times 40$

$⇒ m = 9600kg$
